rounds.name: Online Assessment
rounds.description: Test conducted on Hackerrank for 90 minutes with 3 sections: 1 DSA, 2 SQL, 2 REST API questions. DSA question: check whether a password was strong or weak. SQL section with two complex queries. REST API section required creating a GET method from scratch.

questions.text: Check whether a password is strong or weak based on conditions like containing only lowercase or uppercase letters, only numericals, or containing a substring present in a banned_words list.
Create a GET method using any language (C, C++, Java, JavaScript, Python) from scratch, hit a URL to get data, apply a given filter and return the filtered data.

rounds.name: Technical Round
rounds.description: Three‑panel interview focusing on technical skills, projects and internships. Questions covered OOP concepts in Java, a DSA transaction‑validation problem, SQL queries on Employee and Department schemas, JWT, REST API methods, and project details.

questions.text: Explain polymorphism, diamond problem, how interfaces solve the diamond problem, static keyword, differences between static variables and static methods in Java.

Given a list of transactions (description, credit, debit, current balance) with an initial balance, flag any transactions where the current balance is incorrect. Use string functions like split and parseInt.
Write three SQL queries on Employee and Department schemas using joins, group by, aggregate functions, and subqueries (WITH clause).
Describe JWT, its structure, and how it was implemented in the candidate’s project.
Explain differences between GET, PUT, and POST REST API methods and whether a new entry can be created using a GET request.

tips.text: Maintain a good CGPA (at least 8) to be shortlisted for the OA.
Pay attention in PPT and interact with the company employees so that they remember you.
PLEASE TAKE SQL SERIOUSLY, IT SEEMS EASY UNTIL IT ISN’T, SO PRACTISING SQL IS VERY IMPORTANT.
Prepare a good 1‑2 min introduction beforehand, use ChatGPT or other AI tools to refine it.
Follow Striver’s sheet for DSA, give contests on LeetCode, CodeChef, Codeforces to build habit of solving under time pressure.
Aptitude is very important; practice timed tests to mimic the test environment.
Practice puzzles from GeeksForGeeks to improve critical thinking.
Practice system design questions from GeeksForGeeks.
Practice giving answers in front of a mirror or do mock interviews with friends to improve communication skills.
During interviews, maintain eye contact, stay calm, and ask for help if required.
Remember to fill all required application forms while applying; missing forms can disqualify you.
Keep an eye on hackathons (e.g., Nomura, JPMC, Morgan Stanley, Adobe) as many companies hire through them.
